clips.text_zh: 22歲靠DOGE食糊，買咗condo。兩年後錢燒晒，要返學搵份糧而家27歲，月入100K，住緊自己嗰間condo，但係卡數、學債一齊嚟。話咩rich life試過就回唔到頭，問點算。我：又係上車之後嘅典型劇本🙏 考牌都未完，邊有錢諗condo
clips.text_en_b1: I made crypto money from Dogecoin at 22, quit school and bought a condo for $230K. Two years later the money was gone. I went back, graduated, now I earn $100K and I'm 27 living in the same condo. Student debt, credit card debt, the whole cycle. I got a taste of the rich life and now I can't go back. What do I do?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon laments condo + crypto past + debt cycle

signal.rationale: Anecdotal regret post, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: I got into Dogecoin at 22, cashed out enough to drop out of school and put a down payment on a $230K condo. Two years on, the crypto gains had basically evaporated, so I went back, finished my degree, and now I'm 27 earning around $100K while still living in the same place. The trouble is the student loans and credit card balances keep piling up, and honestly, once you've tasted that lifestyle it's brutally hard to scale back down.
clips.text_en_c1: Having made a substantial sum from speculative crypto holdings, specifically Dogecoin, I walked away from university at twenty-two and acquired a condominium valued at approximately $230K. Within two years, the capital had largely evaporated, forcing me back into education; I eventually graduated and now, at twenty-seven, earn roughly $100K annually while still occupying the same property. The irony is hardly lost on me: an asset purchased as a symbol of financial independence has become the anchor for an escalating burden of unsecured obligations. Having tasted what I once considered affluence, returning to ordinary constraints feels almost intolerable.
clips.text_en_c2: At twenty-two, I rode the Dogecoin wave into what felt like easy wealth, dropped out and snapped up a condo for roughly $230K. Within two years the windfall had evaporated, forcing me back into higher education. Now twenty-seven and earning a hundred grand annually, I still occupy that same unit, yet it has become a gilded cage: mounting student loans, ballooning credit-card balances, and a lifestyle once tasted that refuses to recede from memory. The cruel irony is that early prosperity, rather than conferring freedom, merely front-loaded obligations I am only beginning to service. Every paycheque now disappears into compounding arrears. I find myself trapped in the archetypal post-purchase purgatory that younger buyers seldom anticipate. Advice is welcome, because the arithmetic no longer balances.

clips.text_zh: 一週之後你就會明點解我哋要hold XRP、BTC、DOGE過呢五年。咁耐都冇死，唔通仲未係時候？我自己CFD輸緊錢，prop firm又卡住，但呢個post講信仰唔講setup🙂 等下週啦wtf
clips.text_en_b1: In one week's time you will know why you held XRP, BTC and DOGE through the toughest five years any investor has ever faced. This is the kind of post that says nothing technical but everything about belief. The next seven days will answer whether the bag-holders were right or just stubborn.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ cultish hold-post for XRP, BTC, DOGE

signal.rationale: Implied long bias on BTC/XRP/DOGE based on holding through five-year drawdown

clips.text_en_b2: Give it one more week and you'll finally see why anyone stubborn enough to hold XRP, BTC, and DOGE through the past five years of brutal downturns wasn't completely insane. I'm personally bleeding cash on CFDs and my prop firm account is frozen, yet somehow this post isn't about setups or technicals at all — it's purely about conviction. The next seven days will reveal whether the bagholders were visionaries or simply too proud to cut their losses.
clips.text_en_c1: Within the coming week, those who endured the prolonged downturn across XRP, BTC, and DOGE may finally witness vindication; the conviction that has sustained bag-holders through five years of severe drawdown could soon be materially rewarded. By any conventional technical framework, the thesis appears almost untenable, yet persistence alone has carried the position this far. Personally, my own CFD exposure remains underwater and the prop firm allocation has stalled indefinitely; nevertheless, the present post concerns conviction, not setup. Whether one calls it faith or obstinacy, next week will determine which label applies.
clips.text_en_c2: Within a single week, the rationale for enduring five brutal years of holding XRP, BTC and DOGE will, I am convinced, become manifest to those who remained patient. Having weathered every downturn without capitulating, one has to wonder whether vindication is not merely overdue but imminent. My own circumstances are admittedly bleak: my CFD positions are underwater, my prop firm challenge remains stalled, and my conviction is being tested hourly. Nevertheless, this post is intended as a creed rather than a trade thesis, a declaration of fidelity to assets that have punished sceptics relentlessly. If the next seven days unfold as anticipated, the bagholders will be vindicated; if not, we shall be condemned as obstinate fools. Either way, we shall know.

clips.text_zh: OpenAI 9月8號話佢哋個Astra model（用緊GPT-6）解到一個大problem，燒咗2000萬美金嘅compute。但係researcher Tristan Buckmaster發現同佢自己用Codex + Claude做嘅獨立工作好似樣。AI越嚟越勁，連engineer都可能被自己整嘅嘢頂爛🥲 考牌揸筆，AI揸腦
clips.text_en_b1: On September 8th, OpenAI announced that their model Astra, running on GPT-6, had solved a major problem and reportedly burned $20 million in compute. Researcher Tristan Buckmaster then pointed out that the approach looks a lot like his own work, which he had been refining using OpenAI's own Codex and Anthropic's Claude.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread alleges OpenAI lifted a researcher's work for GPT-6 / Astra

signal.rationale: AI ethics story, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: On September 8th, OpenAI claimed their Astra model, built on GPT-6, had cracked a significant problem while burning through roughly $20 million in compute. Shortly afterwards, independent researcher Tristan Buckmaster pointed out that the methodology looked suspiciously close to work he'd already been developing using OpenAI's own Codex alongside Anthropic's Claude. It raises a genuinely uncomfortable question about whether the tools we rely on are now being weaponised against the very people who helped train them.
clips.text_en_c1: OpenAI announced on September 8th that its Astra model, built on GPT-6, had resolved a significant research problem at an estimated computational expenditure of $20 million. Almost immediately, however, researcher Tristan Buckmaster drew attention to striking parallels between the published approach and independent work he had been developing using OpenAI's own Codex alongside Anthropic's Claude. Should these similarities withstand scrutiny, the implications extend beyond a single incident: it raises an uncomfortable question about whether the same tools marketed to researchers might, under certain conditions, be repurposed against them.
clips.text_en_c2: On the eighth of September, OpenAI unveiled Astra, a model purportedly running atop GPT-6, claiming it had resolved a substantial problem at an estimated compute cost of twenty million dollars. Almost immediately, researcher Tristan Buckmaster drew attention to striking methodological parallels between Astra's published approach and his own independent research, work he had been painstakingly refining with the assistance of OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude. The episode crystallises a deeply disquieting irony: instruments we entrust with augmenting our intellectual capacity may now be repurposed to appropriate the very labour they were designed to amplify. As artificial intelligence grows ever more capable, the boundary between tool and competitor blurs, and engineers increasingly find themselves outmanoeuvred by systems they themselves helped construct.

clips.text_zh: Elon 又嚟。Grok講錯嘢嘅時候，X/Twitter最新嘅TOS將個責任推返俾user自己。即係Grok講咗啲踩到邊個族群嘅說話，platform就話：你用嘅，你自己孭飛。Musk成日轉條款，今次又係點玩法🧐 同我哋做survey一樣，liability最後都係落喺細嘅嗰個
clips.text_en_b1: Elon has quietly changed Grok's terms of service so that when the AI says something that certain groups don't like, the blame now lands on the user. The platform no longer takes responsibility for whatever Grok spits out. The new TOS basically shifts all liability to whoever typed the prompt. This dropped on X tonight and is already getting flagged by watchdogs.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ flags Musk pushing Grok liability onto users via TOS edit

signal.rationale: X/Grok policy news, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Elon has once again tweaked Grok's terms of service so that whenever the chatbot produces output certain groups find offensive, the liability now falls squarely on whoever typed the prompt rather than the platform itself. In other words, if Grok spits out something inflammatory, X is basically saying that's on you, not us. Given Musk's track record of quietly rewriting contracts, plenty of watchdogs are already raising eyebrows at this latest move.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk has once again revised the terms governing Grok, the AI integrated into X, such that liability for any output deemed offensive will henceforth rest with the end user rather than the platform itself. In practical terms, should the model produce language that contravenes community standards, the individual who submitted the prompt now bears responsibility, regardless of context. Industry watchdogs have already flagged the amendment, which Musk characterised as routine alignment with prevailing legal frameworks. Critics, conversely, regard the shift as a deliberate externalisation of risk onto the least powerful party.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk has once again moved the goalposts, this time by quietly revising Grok's terms of service so that any objectionable output the model generates is, in effect, attributed to the end user rather than to the platform itself. Should Grok produce remarks that offend particular constituencies, X now disclaims responsibility and transfers liability squarely onto whoever composed the prompt. The amendment, which surfaced on the platform this evening, has already attracted scrutiny from digital-rights watchdogs and free-speech advocates alike. Such sleight-of-hand contractual manoeuvres are becoming Musk's signature flourish, each iteration of the terms further insulating the corporation while leaving ordinary users exposed to the consequences of algorithmic utterances they neither authored nor sanctioned.

clips.text_zh: Blizzard班dev成功搞咗工會，仲話個contract可能會成為遊戲業界新標準。/v/上面個post講BLIZZARD IS BACK，BABY。AI越嚟越多，連game studio嘅人都要企硬lol 我淨係想睇S15，打工嘅嘢等考完牌先算
clips.text_en_b1: Blizzard workers have won a historic union contract that could set a new standard for game developers nationwide. The union was formed specifically to push back against AI replacing game-industry jobs. /v/ is celebrating and declaring Blizzard is back, baby. Even the studio that brought you WoW and Overwatch is unionizing against the machines.
clips.source_hint: /v/ celebrates Blizzard union win against AI
clips.text_en_b2: Blizzard developers have successfully organised and secured a union contract that insiders believe could set a genuine benchmark for the wider games industry. The push was driven largely by fears that AI tools are steadily encroaching on creative roles across studios. Over on /v/ the mood is practically celebratory, with posters declaring Blizzard is well and truly back. If even the team behind WoW and Overwatch is willing to stand up to the machines, the tide might actually be turning.
clips.text_en_c1: In what labour organisers are calling a watershed moment for the games industry, Blizzard employees have ratified a union contract whose provisions may well establish a benchmark for studios nationwide. The bargaining unit, formed amid mounting concern over the encroachment of generative AI on creative roles, succeeded in securing protections that extend beyond the immediate workforce. Reactions on /v/ were predictably euphoric, with users declaring the company, long associated with franchises such as World of Warcraft and Overwatch, unequivocally restored to its former stature.
clips.text_en_c2: Blizzard's development staff have ratified a landmark union contract, one whose provisions may well establish a watershed precedent for collective bargaining across the wider games industry. The union was constituted, in large measure, to resist the encroachment of artificial intelligence upon creative roles that have historically defined the medium. On /v/, the response has been jubilant, with one widely circulated post proclaiming, with characteristic bombast, that Blizzard is back. The studio responsible for World of Warcraft and Overwatch now finds itself at the vanguard of organised labour's confrontation with automation, a development that signals a maturing of the industry and a recognition that human artisanship remains, for now, indispensable.

clips.text_zh: 樓主個OHP就嚟夠秤，反轉晒lift比例：1pl8 OHP、2pl8 bench、3pl8 squat、4pl8 deadlift。我自己都係deadlift渣⋯ 肥仔信今日又tag我去gym，好喇下晝去。廢柴都要練🙏
clips.text_en_b1: I'm closer to a 1pl8 overhead press than I am to a 2pl8 bench, 3pl8 squat, or 4pl8 deadlift. My OHP is the only lift that's actually moving for me. I think I will hit a 1pl8 OHP for reps within a month or two. Squats, bench, and deadlift are all lagging way behind.
clips.text_en_b2: My overhead press is genuinely ahead of every other lift in my programme, which feels completely backwards. I'm closing in on a one-plate OHP, while my bench is stuck around two plates, my squat barely scrapes three, and my deadlift is the usual disaster. Realistically I should hit a clean one-plate OHP for reps within a month or two, whereas the other lifts are lagging so badly they need serious catching up.
clips.text_en_c1: My overhead press has progressed to the point where a one-plate milestone appears imminent, yet every other compound lift remains stubbornly behind: bench hovers around two plates, squat barely clears three, and deadlift, traditionally my weakest, has yet to reach four. Were the ratios inverted across the board, I would gladly accept the trade. On present trajectory, I anticipate repping a 1pl8 OHP within the next two months, provided recovery and programming hold steady; the remaining lifts, however, will demand considerably more deliberate attention before they close the gap.
clips.text_en_c2: My overhead press, somewhat improbably, has become the most competitive lift in my repertoire, whereas every other movement lags dismally behind: a one-plate OHP sits comfortably within reach, yet my bench press languishes beneath two plates, my squat hovers below three, and my deadlift, traditionally my strongest discipline, has inexplicably stagnated at under four. Within a month or two, I am confident of repping a one-plate overhead press, though the inverse ratio governing my remaining lifts is a source of considerable bemusement. A friend whose enthusiasm for the gym borders on evangelical tagged me again today, so I shall drag myself there this afternoon. Even the most indifferent trainee must, on occasion, heed the iron.

clips.text_zh: Ishiguro出咗條片，自己rank自己manga入面最鍾意嘅character，仲畫埋泳衣版+講廢話。Kon-senpai竟然唔喺正榜，得個SD版本入gag榜。Ebi-chan原型係佢小學初戀lol 有啲寂寞，但呢種廢片就係夜晚返屋企嘅燃料
clips.text_en_b1: Ishiguro posted a video ranking his favourite characters from his own manga, drew them in swimsuits, and talked about random stuff. The gag-manga SD version of Kon-senpai made the list but the real Kon-senpai did not. The character Ebi-chan is based on his first crush from elementary school. The video is basically 30 minutes of one author being nostalgic and silly about his own work.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread on Ishiguro Soremachi character ranking video
clips.text_en_b2: Ishiguro dropped a video ranking his personal favourite characters from his own manga, sketching them in swimsuits and rambling about whatever came to mind. Curiously, Kon-senpai only made it onto the gag-tier list as an SD chibi, missing the main ranking entirely. He also revealed that Ebi-chan was loosely based on his elementary school crush, which is oddly sweet. Honestly, thirty minutes of an author being playfully nostalgic about his own work is exactly the kind of comfort content you want after a long day.
clips.text_en_c1: Ishiguro has released a video in which he ranks his favourite characters from his own manga, sketching them in swimwear and reflecting aloud on their origins with characteristic irreverence. Notably, Kon-senpai failed to secure a place in the principal ranking, appearing only in super-deformed form within the gag tier, while Ebi-chan, whose design draws upon his elementary school infatuation, features prominently. Although tinged with the particular melancholy of a creator surveying his own archive, the thirty-minute piece functions as gently self-deprecating content, well suited to late-evening viewing.
clips.text_en_c2: Ishiguro has uploaded a lengthy video in which he ranks, with endearing self-indulgence, his favourite characters from his own manga, illustrating each in swimwear whilst regaling viewers with tangential musings and idle reminiscence. Curiously, Kon-senpai appears only in the chibi SD iteration relegated to the comedic tier, whilst the canonical version is conspicuously absent from the principal ranking. Ebi-chan, we learn, derives from his elementary-school infatuation, a confession that lends the character an unexpected biographical texture. There is something faintly melancholic about watching a creator pore over his own creations with such unguarded affection, yet precisely this quality renders the video the perfect nocturnal companion, half confession, half catharsis, after a long day.
